title: Onboard Elysion-Pro-13B v1.1 — perf profiles, metadata, and automated changelog
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: Add Elysion-Pro-13B v1.1 to the model registry with validated performance profiles, updated metadata, and full changelog/release-notes automation. This PR is part of ENG-4231 and the model onboarding checklist for our Q1 catalog refresh. Context: Elysion-Pro v1.1 introduces micro-optimizations to the attention kernel and slightly different tokenizer behavior. We need explicit perf profiles (latency/throughput across GPU types and sequence lengths), updated metadata (sources, model card, quantization recommendations), and an automated changelog entry so downstream consumers (hosted, dedicated, private) see the versioned release notes. Changes: - Add new model directory models/elysion-pro/13b/v1.1 containing model.json, model-card.md, and packing metadata. - Add perf profiles to perf-profiles/elysion-pro/13b/v1.1/*.json for g4dn, a100, and v100 targets with sequence-length buckets 64/256/1024. Profiles include p50/p95 latency and tokens/s throughput. - Extend changelog automation to pick up newly added model metadata and append a generated note to the curated changelog (changelogs/models.yaml) via scripts/changelog-generator/registry-hook.py. - Update registry index to reference v1.1 and add compatibility tags (tokenizer-updated, attention-optim). - Add unit and integration tests for model metadata validation and perf profile schema. Rollout plan: After merge we'll trigger the registry publish job which runs a quick smoke inference on dedicated test hardware (a100) and uploads validation artifacts to artifacts.redwood.ai. We'll then schedule a canary promoted to hosted catalog next week pending monitoring. Backwards compatibility: This is additive only; v1.1 is registered as a separate model version and old version remains available. The tokenizer change is backwards-compatible for typical prompts; we include a migration note in the model-card. Commits: See commit summary below. CI: All checks passed on the final run. The changelog-generator test initially failed on a JSON schema edge case (missing edition field) and was fixed in a follow-up commit. Related: references PM-981 for product release messaging and SUP-1120 for a customer request to expose latency buckets for pricing calculations.
